title: MCP
description: Plug Claude into GitHub, databases, browsers and more with the Model Context Protocol.

lessons.title: What Is MCP?
lessons.description: Servers that give Claude new tools

theory.title: A universal plug for tools
theory.body:
**MCP** stands for **Model Context Protocol**: an open standard for connecting AI tools like Claude Code to external systems and data.

An **MCP server** is a small program that exposes **tools** Claude can call. Connect the GitHub server and Claude can read issues and open PRs. Connect a database server and it can query your tables. Connect Playwright and it can drive a real browser.

Every tool gets a name in the pattern `mcp__<server>__<tool>`: the word `mcp`, the server's name, the tool's name, joined by **two** underscores. You'll see these names in Claude's output and in permission rules.

Kip's take: MCP is like bolting new limbs onto the shell. Same crab, many more claws.
theory.code:
# server named "github", tool named "list_issues"
mcp__github__list_issues

# server named "db", tool named "query"
mcp__db__query

theory.title: Local vs remote servers
theory.body:
How Claude talks to a server is called its **transport**. You'll type these names in lowercase:

`stdio` ("standard input/output"): the server runs as a **local** program on your machine, started by a command such as `npx ...`. Claude talks to it through that program's input and output.

`http`: the server lives at a **URL** on the internet. This is the recommended option for remote services. The older `sse` transport is deprecated, so avoid it.

Only add servers you trust. A server that fetches outside content (web pages, issues, emails) could hand Claude hidden instructions written by someone else. That attack is called **prompt injection**.
theory.code:
stdio -> local program on your machine
http  -> remote server at a URL (recommended for remote)
sse   -> old remote transport, deprecated

exercises.explanation: MCP is the Model Context Protocol: a shared standard, so any tool that speaks it can plug into Claude the same way.

exercises.prompt: What does connecting an MCP server give Claude?
options: New tools and data sources from an external system
exercises.explanation: A server adds tools, not intelligence: it gives Claude new actions it can take in an outside system.

exercises.prompt: Match each MCP server to what it lets Claude do.
exercises.explanation: Each server plugs Claude into one external system, so you add the server for whichever system you need Claude to reach.

exercises.prompt: You're connecting to a remote MCP server hosted at a URL. Which transport is recommended?
exercises.explanation: HTTP is the recommended transport for remote servers because SSE is deprecated and stdio only works for programs on your own machine.

exercises.prompt: Tools from an MCP server named `github` appear to Claude with names like…
exercises.explanation: MCP tools follow mcp__<server>__<tool> so tools from different servers never clash, and you use the same name in permission rules.

exercises.prompt: Why should you only add MCP servers you trust?
options: Servers that fetch outside content can expose you to prompt injection
Claude can only connect to one server at a time
exercises.explanation: Content a server pulls in could contain instructions written by a stranger, so a server is only as safe as what it fetches.

exercises.prompt: The GitHub MCP server is connected. You want help with issue #142 in acme/web.
options: Use the GitHub MCP server to read issue #142 in acme/web, summarize the bug, then propose a fix for src/cart.ts. Don't edit anything yet.
exercises.explanation: Naming the server, repo, issue and file tells Claude which tool to call and where to look, instead of guessing.

exercises.code:
MCP stands for Model ___ Protocol.
Local servers run as a process and talk over ___.
Remote servers are best connected over ___.
exercises.hint: Local program on your machine = stdio. Server at a URL = http.
exercises.explanation: The transport depends on where the server runs: stdio for a program on your machine, http for one at a URL.

exercises.scenario: A read-only Postgres MCP server named `db` is connected. Signups dropped last week and you want Claude to investigate without changing anything.
exercises.sample: Context: daily signups dropped sharply sometime last week, and the db MCP server is connected (read-only). Goal: find when the drop started and what might explain it. Use db to query daily signups for the last 14 days and show where the drop begins. Then read @src/signup/handler.ts and list recent logic that could explain it. Constraints: read-only queries only, and don't edit any code. Done when you report the query you ran, the first day of the drop, and up to 3 suspects with line numbers.
exercises.explanation: Great MCP prompts name the server, the exact data to pull, what Claude must not touch, and what the finished report looks like.

theory.title: Reading claude mcp add
theory.body:
You add servers from your normal shell (not inside a Claude session). The shape is: `claude mcp add`, then any **options**, then a **name** you choose, then where the server is.

**Remote server**: `--transport http` (short `-t http`), a name, then the URL.

**Local stdio server**: a name, then `--`, then the command that launches the server. stdio is the default, so `--transport stdio` is optional. The `--` means "Claude's options end here": everything after it is handed to the server untouched, even things that look like flags, such as `--port 8080`.

`npx @playwright/mcp@latest` is a launch command: `npx` runs a Node package without installing it for good, and `@latest` asks for the newest version.

Options like `--transport`, `--scope` and `-e KEY=value` (an environment variable, often a secret) go **before** the name.
theory.code:
# remote:  claude mcp add --transport http <name> <url>
claude mcp add --transport http notion https://mcp.notion.com/mcp

# local:   claude mcp add <name> -- <launch command>
claude mcp add playwright -- npx @playwright/mcp@latest

# options first, then name, then url
claude mcp add --transport http --scope project notion https://mcp.notion.com/mcp

theory.title: Managing servers and scopes
theory.body:
Three shell commands manage what you've added: `claude mcp list` (all servers), `claude mcp get <name>` (one server's details), `claude mcp remove <name>` (delete it).

Inside a session, the slash command `/mcp` shows each server's status. Kip checks it for the word `connected`. Many remote servers need you to log in with **OAuth**: you pick the server in `/mcp`, a browser opens, you sign in there, and no password is ever pasted into Claude.

`--scope` decides who gets a server: `local` (the default) is just you in this project; `project` writes it to `.mcp.json` at the repo root so the team shares it through git; `user` is just you, in every project.
theory.code:
claude mcp list
claude mcp get notion
claude mcp remove notion

# inside a session
> /mcp

theory.title: Inside .mcp.json
theory.body:
A project-scoped server is saved as JSON in `.mcp.json`. Part by part:

`"mcpServers"`: the one top-level key; every server lives inside it.

`"notion"`: the server's name (the same name you gave `claude mcp add`).

`"type": "http"`: the transport. `"url"`: where the remote server lives.

A local server uses `"command"` and an `"args"` list instead of a URL.

exercises.prompt: In `claude mcp add myserver -- python server.py --port 8080`, what does the `--` do?
options: Comments out the rest of the line
Separates Claude's own options from the server's command and args
Runs the server in the background
exercises.explanation: Without `--`, Claude would try to read `--port 8080` as its own option, so `--` hands everything after it to the server untouched.

exercises.prompt: Match each scope to who gets the server.
exercises.explanation: Pick the scope by who needs the server: only project scope writes a file the team receives through git.

exercises.prompt: Add Notion as a remote server and share it with your team.
exercises.code: claude mcp add ___ http ___ project notion https://mcp.notion.com/mcp
exercises.hint: Options go before the name: --transport http picks the transport, --scope project shares it.
exercises.explanation: `--transport http` is needed because the server is at a URL, and `--scope project` saves it to `.mcp.json` so teammates get it too.

exercises.prompt: Complete this project-scoped config file at the repo root.
exercises.hint: All servers live under one top-level key; a server with a url uses the remote transport.
exercises.explanation: Claude only looks for servers under `mcpServers`, and a server reached by `url` must use type `http` because it isn't a local program.

exercises.prompt: Put the steps for connecting a remote server that uses OAuth in order.
steps: Run claude mcp add --transport http notion https://mcp.notion.com/mcp
Run /mcp and select the notion server
Finish the OAuth login in your browser
Confirm it shows connected, then ask Claude to use it
exercises.explanation: The server must be added from the shell before a session can see it, and OAuth login happens inside the session through `/mcp`.

exercises.prompt: Add a local stdio MCP server named playwright whose launch command is `npx @playwright/mcp@latest`.
accepted: claude mcp add --transport stdio playwright -- npx @playwright/mcp@latest
claude mcp add -t stdio playwright -- npx @playwright/mcp@latest
exercises.explanation: The name comes first and the launch command goes after `--`, so Claude knows which part to run as the server.

exercises.prompt: Add GitHub's remote MCP server over HTTP. Name it github; its URL is https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/
accepted: claude mcp add --transport http github https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/
claude mcp add -t http github https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/
exercises.explanation: A server at a URL isn't a local program, so you name the http transport and give the URL instead of a launch command.

exercises.prompt: From your shell, list every MCP server you've configured.
exercises.hint: claude mcp <subcommand>: the one that lists.
exercises.explanation: `claude mcp list` is the quick check that an add actually saved before you start a session.

exercises.prompt: Inside a session, type the slash command that shows your servers' status and lets you log in to one that needs OAuth.
exercises.hint: A slash followed by the protocol's three letters.
exercises.explanation: `/mcp` runs inside the session because that's where Claude actually connects to servers and can open the OAuth login.

exercises.prompt: From your shell, remove the MCP server named notion.
exercises.explanation: Removing a server you no longer use cuts off tools Claude doesn't need, and also clears its stored OAuth login.

mission.title: Plug In a Server
mission.intro: Time to give Kip a new claw. Connect a real MCP server and make Claude use one of its tools.
checklist: Add a trusted server, e.g. claude mcp add playwright -- npx @playwright/mcp@latest
Run claude mcp list to confirm it's configured
Start claude and run /mcp; make sure the server shows connected
Ask Claude to use one of its tools (e.g. open your local dev site and describe the page)
Run claude mcp get <name> to inspect its config
mission.explanation: Connecting a server and calling its tools is the core MCP loop you'll reuse for GitHub, databases and more.

cheatsheet.description: Model Context Protocol: open standard connecting Claude to external tools and data.
Add a local stdio server; its launch command goes after --.
Add a remote HTTP server (recommended for remote).
Who gets the server; local is the default.
Pass an environment variable to the server (also --env).
Check server status and authenticate with OAuth.
Project-scoped servers at the repo root, shared via git.
How MCP tool names appear in permissions and rules.
